requirements:
Component: a printed plastic clamp body, a block with a bore and two prongs above it, tested in compression on a universal testing machine.

Geometry (CAD): geometry.step, in metres; the part is 60.7 x 77.8 x 16.2 mm. Faces are named f<tag> by their face tag in this STEP file. The block has a bore of radius 19.67 mm along z; the two prongs stand above it, and their top faces f17 and f34 lie on the plane y = 33.84 mm. The bottom face f33 lies on the plane y = -43.96 mm.

Material: Formlabs Alpha Fast resin, printed on a Form Studio 1 and post-cured 2 min; linear elastic and isotropic, E = 2.23 GPa (datasheet tensile modulus, default post-cure), Poisson's ratio 0.35 (not on the datasheet: assumed).

Service loads (the test): the machine's upper compression platen presses down (along -y) on the two prong tops, f17 and f34, with a total force of 1000 N, shared evenly over both faces by area.

Installation and supports (the test machine): the bottom face f33 stands on the lower compression platen, which does not move, and is held on it without slipping or lifting. Nothing else touches the part.

Analysis scope: static, linear elastic, small deformations, no gravity; a solid (three-dimensional) model of the whole part. There is no reference solution: the physical test of this part is the only check.

Required result: u_top, the mean y-displacement of the two prong tops, in m (negative: they move down).

mapping.implied_by: f33 stands on the immovable lower platen, held without slipping or lifting.
1000 N total along -y on f17 and f34, shared evenly by area.
A solid model of the whole part.
